claims.text: Laser surface alloying with 2–5 wt% aluminum followed by annealing will produce a continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale on a MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloy.
The aluminum addition will be incorporated into an approximately 50 μm near-surface region.
The treatment will significantly improve the alloy's high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Post-alloying annealing can ensure uniform distribution and integration of aluminum in the alloyed surface region.
The proposed treatment will be effective during exposure to flowing air at 1000 °C for 100 hours.
Flowing air at 1000 °C for 100 hours is representative of extreme-temperature structural applications.
Locally enriched aluminum oxidizes during high-temperature exposure to form Al2O3.
The resulting Al2O3 layer is dense and stable.
The Al2O3 layer acts as a diffusion barrier that limits oxygen ingress into the substrate.
Limiting oxygen ingress protects the underlying refractory matrix from further oxidation.
Annealing promotes formation of an optimal protective oxide scale.
The treated alloy will have significantly lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will retain strength better than the untreated alloy after oxidation exposure.
The treated alloy will retain creep resistance better than the untreated alloy after oxidation exposure.
The untreated alloy is expected to form a less protective, non-uniform oxide scale under the same exposure conditions.
The untreated alloy is expected to exhibit greater oxidation weight gain than the treated alloy.
Variations in alloy composition or oxidation environment may change the treatment outcome.
